AW-STUDY-0022

Welcome to Abbie’s World

A tour guide meets every new player and asks how they want to start. The grand tour builds a sample world in front of them, then shows it off like a thirty-second commercial, narrated, while the simulation really runs. The last shot eases into the real game, and a few chalk notes follow, drawn beside the real controls and gone as soon as you use them.

Try it in the ranch

Three welcomes

1. The grand tour

The world builds itself, a narrated camera tour of the live ranch (about 30 seconds), then it fades into play and the chalk notes follow. It is also the product tour: toy box, Welcome tour.

2. Show me the basics

Straight into play with chalk notes, one at a time: drag to look around, pick a card, tap anyone to say hi, pause or speed up time, more toys in here.

3. Just let me play

No tips. The guide can be called back any time from the toy box.

Storyboard: the grand tour

Seven stops, hard cuts like a commercial, each camera move measured on the world as it is now (the real goats, the real porch), so the tour never shows something that is not there. A stop whose subject is missing is skipped.

Into the game, then chalk

Shot list

#StopShotSecondsNarratorWhat the world is doing

The tour is a list of stops

Evan’s rule: every new feature decides whether it goes into the tour. A feature joins by registering a stop (a camera shot, a super and a narrator line) or a chalk hint in simulations/welcome/tour-stops.mjs, and the feature brief (docs/design/briefs/feature.md) now asks “Tour: yes or no”. Narration is rendered from those same lines by the welcome-narration workflow (ElevenLabs), with the browser’s voice until it has run.

Design card

Feel“Whoa, I made that, and it’s alive.” Wonder first, then confidence: I know the three things to try. How would a character know?They wouldn’t: the guide, the supers and the chalk are for the player. The world build is the one piece of fiction, and the ranch simply lives (goats wander, lanterns light at dusk). ModeOverlay for the guide and the supers (summoned, one-off); spatial chalk for “tap anyone”; none for the world itself. All on the presentation layer, invisible to every perception. Who it’s forThe player (a new child, or a grown-up seeing the product). What else adaptsTime of day runs to golden hour in the time-lapse, so light, lanterns and people change together. Music waits for the composer to come back; the ranch’s own sound plays.
